rating_distribution.what_happened: Ratings are heavily skewed towards positive scores, with 4.0 (26,818) and 3.0 (20,047) being the most common.
rating_distribution.why_did_it_happen: Users generally self-select movies they anticipate enjoying and tend to avoid or neglect rating movies they dislike.
rating_distribution.why_it_matters: The baseline rating mean is around 3.5. Incorporating a global mean μ and user/movie bias terms in Matrix Factorization is essential to correct for this intrinsic skew.

user_movie_activity.what_happened: Both user engagement and movie popularity exhibit classic power-law / Pareto 'long-tail' distributions.
user_movie_activity.why_did_it_happen: A small fraction of blockbuster films and hyper-active users generate the majority of rating volume, while thousands of niche movies receive very few ratings.
user_movie_activity.why_it_matters: L2 regularization in Matrix Factorization prevents latent embeddings of low-frequency movies and sparse users from overfitting to noise.

top_movies_and_users.what_happened: Films like Forrest Gump, Shawshank Redemption, and Pulp Fiction lead popularity with over 300+ reviews each. The top active user contributed over 2,600 ratings.
top_movies_and_users.why_did_it_happen: Iconic, culturally ubiquitous films receive high natural viewing rates across all demographic segments.
top_movies_and_users.why_it_matters: Popular items have high confidence latent vectors with low variance, providing strong anchor points in the embedding space for collaborative filtering.

highest_rated_threshold.what_happened: Unconstrained top movies are 1-vote anomalies with perfect 5.0 scores. Applying threshold >= 50 reveals universally acclaimed classics (Shawshank Redemption, Godfather, Fight Club).
highest_rated_threshold.why_did_it_happen: Small sample size creates statistical volatility. A single enthusiastic reviewer inflates average rating to maximum.
highest_rated_threshold.why_it_matters: Matrix Factorization naturally penalizes uninformative low-sample movies through movie bias regularization (b_i shrinks toward 0 when data is sparse).

matrix_sparsity.what_happened: 98.30% of the entire user-movie matrix is empty. Even active users have only evaluated a fraction of all available films.
matrix_sparsity.why_did_it_happen: No single individual can watch all 9,700+ movies in a catalog.
matrix_sparsity.why_it_matters: Traditional memory-based collaborative filtering suffers severely in ultra-sparse settings. Low-rank Matrix Factorization solves this by projecting both users and movies into a shared low-dimensional latent space.
